description.text:
Your neurologist handles the medicines. The injections or tablets that keep relapses down, steroids when there's a flare, something for the bladder or the nerve pain. Keep seeing them. Rehab doesn't replace any of that.

But medicine can't teach your legs to trust the stairs again. It won't help you plan a workday so there's still some energy left at 6 pm. heading.text: How Rehabana Helps in Multiple Sclerosis

description.text: No two programmes look the same, but most of them follow roughly these steps.

details.text: We'll watch you walk, get up from a chair, maybe climb a few steps. Then we check strength, balance, stiffness, tiredness, speech and memory, using standard tests. The point is simple. In a month, we can show you numbers instead of just saying "you look better".

You tell us what matters. Walking to the bazaar on Sunday. Going back to office. Having a bath without your daughter waiting outside the door. We take that and work backwards: which therapies, how many days a week, what to practise at home. Your family gets the plan too, explained so it actually makes sense.

Walking, balance, leg strength, stiffness. That's the physio's job. With MS, how much you do matters as much as what you do. Push too hard and you're wiped out for two days. So we start lower than you'd expect and build up. If a walking stick or an ankle splint would keep you safer, we'll tell you.
Dressing. Cooking. Typing. Signing a cheque. OT looks at the jobs you do every day and finds easier ways to do them, plus small changes at home (a shower chair, a higher seat) that save energy.
Voice getting softer? Words a bit slurred? Coughing when you drink tea? Our speech therapist will check it, give you exercises and a few simple rules for eating safely.
Think of energy like money in your wallet. Hard tasks in the morning, rest before you need it, a cool room on hot days, and phone reminders for the things that keep slipping.
For some people, robotic gait training, VR balance games or electrical muscle stimulation help fit in more practice. We use them when they suit your goal, never just for show.
Family members often do too much, out of love. We'll show them how to help safely, and when it's better to wait and let you try.
Every fortnight we repeat the key tests and put them next to your first ones. Then we tell you straight what's improved and what isn't moving yet.

heading.text: FAQs – Multiple Sclerosis Treatment in Kolkata at Rehabana

title.text: Do I need a neurologist before coming to Rehabana?

details.text: Ideally, yes. A neurologist diagnoses MS and handles the medicines. Bring your MRI reports and prescriptions on the first day. Haven't seen one yet? Our doctors can tell you where to start.

title.text: Will rehab replace my MS medicines?

details.text: No, keep taking them. Rehab works next to your medicines. Don't stop or change any of them without asking your neurologist.

title.text: Can I do MS rehab during a relapse?

details.text: Not straight away. In a fresh relapse, rest and medical treatment come first. Once your doctor gives the okay, gentle rehab helps you get back on your feet, and we go by how you feel on the day.

title.text: How often do I need to come for multiple sclerosis rehab in Kolkata?

details.text: It depends on your goals and how much energy you have. Some people come three or four days a week for a few weeks, then cut down and carry on at home. Your doctor will suggest a schedule after the first assessment.

title.text: Will exercise make my MS fatigue worse?

details.text: Usually it's the opposite, if the amount is right. Too much, too soon is what makes it worse. We start small, build in breaks and ask how you felt the next morning.
It depends on how many sessions you need and which therapies. We'll go through the plan and the cost with you before anything starts. Give us a call and we'll explain.

title.text: How do I choose an MS rehabilitation centre in Kolkata?

details.text: Ask a few simple questions before you sign up. Does a rehab doctor (an MD in PMR) actually examine you, or will you only see physios? Do they treat MS and other neuro conditions every week, or mostly back pain and sports injuries? Can you get physio, OT and speech therapy in one place? Will they test you at the start and show you progress on paper? And will they keep your neurologist in the loop? If the answer is yes to most of these, the centre is worth a visit. heading.text: Spinal Cord Injuries and the Rehabilitation Process

description.text: When spinal cord injuries occur due to accidents, falls, disease, or surgery, they cause damage to the spinal cord and disrupt the nerve pathways between the brain and the rest of the body. Whether the condition is acute, subacute, chronic, or related to older spinal trauma, a structured rehabilitation process plays a crucial role in helping individuals gradually regain strength, functional skills, and confidence. heading.text: What Is Motor Neurone Disease (MND) / Motor Neuron Disease?

description.text:
Motor neurone disease is a group of diseases that affects the motor neurones (or motor neurons) – the nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord that control movement. These motor neurons are nerve cells that send signals from your brain to your muscles so you can walk, talk, swallow and breathe.
In MND:

list.text: Upper motor neurons (in the brain) and lower motor neuron cells (in the spinal cord) gradually die.
This loss of motor neurones leads to muscle weakness, stiffness and muscle atrophy (wasting).

Over time, this disease that affects the motor nerves can make everyday tasks harder – walking, climbing stairs, using hands, speaking and swallowing.

Different forms of MND exist, including:
ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) – the most common form of MND, often known as Lou Gehrig's disease.
Progressive bulbar palsy – affecting speech and swallowing early.

Spinal muscular atrophy and Kennedy’s disease – other types of motor neurone disease and neuromuscular disorders.

Because MND is also known by different names in different countries (for example MND Australia and ALS in other places), it can be confusing – but the core problem is similar: upper and lower motor neurons connected to muscles are getting damaged.

heading.text: Types of Motor Neurone Disease & Symptoms of MND

description.text: Doctors describe types of motor neurone disease or types of motor neuron disease based on which motor neurones are most affected and how fast the disease progression is:

list.text: ALS / Motor Neuron Disease – affects both upper and lower motor neurons, causing limb weakness, stiffness, and later speech and breathing problems.
Progressive bulbar palsy – a type of MND where symptoms include early slurred speech, swallowing difficulty and facial weakness.
Primary lateral sclerosis – affects only the upper motor neurons, causing stiffness but less wasting.

Progressive muscular atrophy – mainly affects lower motor neurons connected to muscles, causing marked weakness and muscle atrophy.

These are all forms of MND, and each type of MND can have a different pattern and life expectancy.

heading.text: Symptoms of MND / Symptoms of Motor Neurone Disease

description.text: Motor Neurone Disease (MND) typically begins with subtle symptoms such as a weakened grip, foot dragging, muscle twitching, or slurred speech. As the disease progresses, localized weakness often spreads, leading to generalized muscle stiffness, visible atrophy, and increased difficulty with motor tasks like swallowing or climbing stairs. In advanced stages, the condition can severely impact mobility and respiratory function. The rate of progression varies significantly between individuals, with some experiencing a rapid decline while others remain stable for longer periods.

heading.text: Motor Neuron Disease Treatment – Focus on Care, Comfort & Function

description.text: The exact causes of Motor Neurone Disease (MND), including ALS, remain largely unknown. While a small percentage of cases are linked to inherited genetic mutations, most instances are thought to arise from a complex interplay between genetics and environmental factors, often leaving doctors without a single identifiable cause. Consequently, there is currently no known cure or definitive way to prevent the disease. However, management strategies—such as the medication riluzole, supportive rehabilitation, and various symptom-based treatments—can help slow progression, manage symptoms, and significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.

heading.text: Treatment for Motor Neurone Disease & Treatment for Motor Neuron Disease

description.text: While there is currently no complete cure for Motor Neurone Disease (MND), various medical and supportive interventions can effectively manage the condition. Medications like Riluzole are often prescribed to modestly slow the progression of certain forms of the disease, while other symptom-based drugs address specific issues such as muscle cramps, excess saliva, and pain. Comprehensive rehabilitation and therapy further assist in maintaining motor function and comfort through specialized equipment and planning. Additionally, some patients may access emerging therapies through clinical trials, which continue to advance the treatment landscape and improve daily function for those living with the disease.

heading.text: What is a Traumatic Brain Injury?

description.text:
A traumatic brain injury happens when a sudden injury to the head disrupts normal brain function. This can be due to a closed head injury (something hits your head hard but doesn’t break the skull) or a penetrating head injury (an object enters your brain).

TBI may cause temporary issues, or it can lead to long-term challenges such as brain swelling, damage to the brain tissue, or even brain death in the most severe cases.

Common head injury causes include:

list.text: Road traffic accidents
Falls, especially in older adults
Sports injuries and collisions
Workplace accidents
Assaults or violence
Post-surgical complications

heading.text: Severity of Brain Injuries

description.text: The impact of a TBI depends on injury severity and the area of the brain affected. Doctors typically classify brain injuries into three categories:

details.text: Also called a concussion, mild TBI may cause headaches, dizziness, memory lapses, or confusion. Most patients recover well, but some may still need structured therapy for complete recovery.

details.text: Also called a concussion, mild TBI may cause headaches, dizziness, memory lapses, or confusion. Most patients recover well, but some may still need structured therapy for complete recovery.

description.text: Every patient with a traumatic brain injury (TBI) is different, but symptoms can vary depending on the severity and area of the brain affected. heading.text: How Are Traumatic Brain Injuries Diagnosed?

description.text: At Rehabana, diagnosis begins with compassion and clarity. Families often feel anxious, so our doctors take time to explain every step.

image.alt: Swallowing Problems Are Part of This Too

details.text: We start with a neurological exam to test reflexes, balance, and speech. Families also share details of the injury causes and patient’s medical history.
CT scans or MRIs reveal damage to the brain tissue, swelling of the brain, or a closed head injury. In some cases, doctors detect a diffuse injury or penetrating head injury.
Using the Glasgow Coma Scale, doctors classify cases as mild TBI, moderate TBI, or severe traumatic brain injury.
Memory, problem-solving, and emotional health are evaluated to guide therapy.

primary.subheading: How Brain Injury Impacts Function and Behavior

heading.text: How Does TBI Affect the Brain?

description.text: The brain is delicate, and even a mild traumatic brain injury (TBI) can disrupt normal function. Severe injuries may damage brain cells, brain tissue, or blood flow, leading to physical, cognitive, emotional, and long-term complications. The effects often depend on which area of the brain is affected, which is why treatment must be personalized for each patient.

list.text: Physical impact: Difficulty walking, moving, or performing daily activities.
Cognitive impact: Memory loss, reduced attention span, and slower problem-solving.
Emotional impact: Depression, anxiety, anger, or mood swings.
Long-term risks: Increased risk of neurological conditions later in life.
Frontal lobe injury: May cause personality or behavioral changes.
Temporal lobe injury: May affect speech and memory.
Occipital lobe injury: May lead to vision problems.

heading.text: Why Rehabilitation is Critical After TBI

heading.text: Peripheral Neuropathy in Kolkata

description.text:
Peripheral neuropathy treatment in Kolkata focuses on managing damage to the peripheral nerves — the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. When these nerves are affected, it can impact sensation, movement, or even organ and gland function, depending on whether motor, sensory, or autonomic nerves are involved. Symptoms may develop suddenly or progress slowly over time, and the condition may be reversible or permanent depending on the severity of nerve injury.

The most common cause is diabetes mellitus, but neuropathy can also result from hypothyroidism, vitamin B6 or B12 deficiency, certain medications (including chemotherapy and some antibiotics), radiation therapy, excessive alcohol use, toxin exposure (like lead), autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or SLE, infections, or hereditary conditions like HMSN. Patients often experience burning or stabbing pain in the hands and feet, numbness, muscle weakness, balance problems, walking difficulty, and an increased risk of falls.

Diagnosis is usually based on physical examination and tests such as monofilament testing, nerve conduction studies (NCV), EMG, and sometimes CSF analysis. Medical treatment may include antidepressants, anticonvulsants, vitamins, antioxidants, or immunosuppressants as prescribed by a rehab physician to manage symptoms.

Neurorehabilitation plays a crucial role beyond medication. Through sensory-motor retraining, balance and gait training, electrotherapy, assistive devices, occupational therapy, and home modifications, the focus is on improving mobility, preventing falls, and restoring independence. At Rehabana, our goal is to help you regain function, confidence, and a better quality of life through structured, consistent rehabilitation care.

title.text: How do I book a session at your Animal Assisted Therapy Centre in Kolkata?

details.text: Booking a session is easy. You can call or WhatsApp us at 9088746565, email at rehabana.care@gmail.com, or visit rehabana.com to send an enquiry. Our team will guide you through the next steps and schedule an assessment with our rehab doctors.
